name: Stomata Field
desc: The underside of a leaf under the microscope: pavement cells interlock across the epidermis as wavy jigsaw pieces, their sinuous anticlinal walls fitting lobe into bay, and scattered through them are the stomata -- each a pair of kidney-shaped guard cells flanking a central pore, packed with chloroplasts. The stomata work: guard cells swell and slacken with turgor so their pores open and close, each on its own rhythm plus a slow global light drive, while the chloroplasts stream inside and the whole peel drifts gently under the objective, everything on incommensurate rates so it never re-phases. Offered as a Nomarski DIC peel, confocal fluorescence with red chloroplast autofluorescence, an antique botanical plate, or a false-colour turgor map.

scale.doc: magnification - cells swell, fewer larger, guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: how fast stomata open/close, chloroplasts stream and the peel drifts

density.doc: how finely the epidermis is packed with cells

aperture.doc: how wide the stomatal pores open and how many stomata there are

style.doc: aesthetic: Nomarski DIC leaf-peel relief / confocal fluorescence with red chloroplast autofluorescence / antique botanical plate / false-colour turgor map

seed.doc: deterministic - re-throws cell shapes, stomata placement and chloroplasts
